verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents a token revocation endpoint covering both refresh and access tokens, an introspection endpoint that returns a token's active state, admin-side session management, and single sign-out, which together cover server-side revocation of a compromised session. Session expiry and timeout configuration are never documented in the pack, and refresh is only implied by the existence of refresh tokens. Missing for 10: documented session idle/max expiry configuration, an explicit refresh-token flow and rotation, admin API details for killing a specific session, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage session lifecycle — expiry, refresh, and immediate server-side revocation of a compromised session

citations.quote: The token revocation endpoint is used to revoke tokens. Both refresh tokens and access tokens are supported by this endpoint.
The introspection endpoint is used to retrieve the active state of a token. In other words, you can use it to validate an access or refresh token.
They can also manage users, including permissions and sessions.
Keycloak provides single-sign out, which means users only have to logout once to be logged-out of all applications that use Keycloak.
